This innovative attraction includes interactive installations that combine scents, sounds, and historical narratives. After three years of development with Digital Kitchen, the mansion’s historical essence is preserved while incorporating QR codes to provide deeper insights. The Preservation Society aims to enrich visitor experiences and modernize storytelling in historic homes, ensuring educational significance remains intact.

title: 'Bring them back': To end terror, Shah pushes to hunt down fugitives hiding abroad
description: Amit Shah emphasized the need for international cooperation in the fight against terrorism and organized crime, specifically calling for the return of offenders hiding abroad. He pointed out important milestones, such as the dismantling of the Popular Front of India network. The ongoing two-day Anti-Terror Conference aims to foster intelligence sharing and strengthen investigations, ultimately enhancing inter-agency collaboration to tackle evolving security threats.

title: WTC Points Table: South Africa dethrone New Zealand; where does India stand?
description: Following a decisive win against Bangladesh, South Africa has surged to the pinnacle of the World Test Championship standings, boasting an impressive points percentage of 75. title: COP31's paradox: A vow to fight global warming but silent on fossil fuels
description: The revised COP31 agreement notably omits any mentions of fossil fuels, sparking fears regarding its impact on climate commitments. Released from negotiations in Antalya, Turkey, this draft reveals sharp divides among participating nations, with some pushing for definitive measures to phase out fossil fuels while others cling to energy security.

title: 18-year-old Argentine footballer dies after head injury during youth match
description: Argentine football is mourning 18-year-old Abel Nunez, who died two days after suffering a devastating head injury during a youth match between FC Ezeiza and Deportivo Muniz. Struck by a powerful clearance from close range, Nunez collapsed and required emergency surgery for a fractured skull and internal bleeding. Both clubs have since paid tribute to the teenager.

title: Mahadev betting app case: Saurabh Chandrakar sent to judicial custody till Dec 2
description: Saurabh Chandrakar has been sent to judicial custody until December 2 by a special court in Raipur. The Enforcement Directorate indicated that it does not require further custodial interrogation at this point. Chandrakar was extradited from Oman earlier this month and produced before the court after a CBI operation. Allegations suggest he operated an illegal online betting network earning significant amounts monthly since 2020.

Etihad Airways ordered to pay Rs 30,000 after passenger's 8-day baggage ordeal
description: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission issued a ruling against Etihad Airways regarding an international passenger's missing baggage. Alfred Varghese traveled on an eight-day pilgrimage and experienced a delivery issue with his checked-in baggage. Although the airline apologized and offered minimal compensation, the commission found the airline liable for service deficiency. Varghese's claim of unfair trade practice was rejected due to lack of evidence for emergency expenditures.

title: 'Did you hire more, hike salaries?' PM tears into 'hunger' of bizmen despite tax cut
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday urged industry leaders to prioritise employee compensation and expand their workforce. He cited governmental efforts to bolster the business climate, such as lowering corporate taxes and simplifying tax regulations. PM Modi also emphasised the importance of maintaining high product standards, and reducing reliance on imported pharmaceuticals to fortify local industries.

title: Trump’s heir, but not his echo: JD Vance, Iran and the limits of loyalty
description: JD Vance’s metamorphosis from Donald Trump's critic to his deputy reflects the complexities of the Republican political agenda. Both men share similar views on economic nationalism and immigration policies. Vance, however, has shown more scepticism toward military involvement and American commitments abroad. Recent elections highlighted the potential political consequences of the Iran war, impacting their positions.

title: Auston Matthews’ post-game comments raise fresh concerns over Maple Leafs’ future
description: Auston Matthews has delivered an ominous message after the Toronto Maple Leafs’ loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. The skipper feels the squad has the talent to compete but stressed that the performances must improve. With Toronto struggling in the Atlantic Division, his comments have intensified questions about the team's leadership, management decisions, and ability to return to contention.

title: 'Pakistan used bottle tops, not sandpaper': Shoaib Akhtar after Khawaja's claims
description: Shoaib Akhtar has reacted to Usman Khawaja's fresh ball-tampering claims, urging people not to make a fuss over the 2018 Sandpapergate controversy. Akhtar admitted Pakistan also tampered with cricket balls, using "bottle tops, not sandpaper". He also backed Khawaja's claim that Australia's entire team knew about the incident, while questioning his timing and decision to expose former teammates.

The impact is predominantly felt by engineers and technical staff, who are struggling to secure visas, in contrast to the smoother process for marketing employees. This is not an isolated incident, as last year's CES also witnessed similar challenges. Nevertheless, AgiBot and Unitree plan to move forward with attendance.

title: Ukraine's bridge blitz: Kyiv targets Russia's Crimea rail lifeline with Neptune missiles
description: Ukraine has targeted the Kerch Bridge, damaging the railway lifeline connecting Crimea to Russia. The attack used Neptune missiles, disrupting train traffic and prompting assessments of the damage. Previous strikes on the bridge earlier in the week had already caused significant disruption and casualties. The Kerch Bridge serves as a crucial transport route for both civilian and military logistics.

An exciting proposal also emerged for an Innovation Hub in India to strengthen technological collaborations.

title: Sikh family preserves Sonia Gandhi's ancestral home in Italian village
description: Sukhdev Singh Kang has purchased the ancestral home of Sonia Gandhi located in Italy and intends to open a museum. The property, identified as Sonia Gandhi's birthplace, has garnered significant interest from Indian visitors. Kang's family aims to preserve her family's history through artifacts and personal items displayed at the museum. They also plan to meet with Sonia Gandhi and her children to enrich the museum experience.

title: Salesforce senior manager’s ‘layoff post’ on LinkedIn goes viral: Read what it says

Previous job cuts included approximately 4,000 roles lost last year due to automated AI tools. These workforce reductions have occurred during a period of investor concern regarding AI's impact on software businesses.

title: 'Saddened by the news': Stalin mourns VS Babu, who unseated him in Kolathur
Record! Chahal becomes first Indian bowler to cross historic milestone
description: Yuzvendra Chahal became the first Indian bowler to take 400 T20 wickets, reaching the milestone while playing for Haryana against Tamil Nadu in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. The 36-year-old finished with 3/16, taking his tally to 402 wickets in 246 matches. He now leads all Indian bowlers in T20 wickets, ahead of Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Jasprit Bumrah.

title: 10,000 Rohingya killed, mass rapes: UN court delivers landmark Myanmar genocide verdict
description: In a significant ruling, the International Court of Justice revealed that Myanmar's military was responsible for the deaths of around 10,000 Rohingya Muslims in 2017. This decision emphasized the genocidal intent behind the military's actions and highlighted instances of severe sexual violence and brutality against children. Gambia accused Myanmar of breaching the 1948 Genocide Convention, demanding reparations, while Myanmar dismissed these claims as counterterrorism measures.

title: '140 clicks was hard to come by': Shastri questions pace attack, asks 'Where was Siraj?'
description: Ravi Shastri expressed his apprehensions regarding the omission of Mohammed Siraj from India's first Test lineup. India initially excelled, reducing New Zealand to a precarious 70/5, thanks to Jasprit Bumrah's stellar bowling. Nonetheless, a resilient partnership between Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips lifted New Zealand to a solid 243/5 by the day's conclusion.

title: Arkansas man, 82, lived on 331 family acres for 30+ years; court rejects appeal
description: William J Cooper, an 82-year-old resident, faced significant hurdles in selling his family's inherited land as ordered by the court. Although he sought a physical division to continue living there, the Arkansas Court of Appeals ultimately deemed his appeal moot after the property was sold to a third party. This case highlights the complex challenges heirs may encounter in property disputes.

title: Infantino remains favourite as FIFA president gets two challengers for 2027 vote
description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino is poised to run for re-election in 2027, facing opponents Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima. Diallo, who has garnered support from UEFA member associations, recently declared his candidacy. Meanwhile, Tashima entered the race with his nomination earlier this month. Despite some concerns regarding his eligibility, Infantino, in office since 2016, remains the frontrunner. The electoral committee will finalise candidate lists by February 18, 2027.

title: BS-I to BS-VI vehicles get new PUC certificate validity periods; check yours
description: The ministry of road transport and highways recently unveiled revised regulations concerning pollution under control certificates. The new guidelines offer longer validity for BS-VI vehicles based on their age and usage while mandating more frequent emission checks for older vehicles. Furthermore, there will be a standardised validity period for older emission categories throughout India, enhancing compliance and promoting uniformity in emission standards.

Right to breathe: Can you take the government to court over polluted air?
description: Air pollution remains a major issue affecting cities across India, with Delhi and Mumbai reporting concerning air quality levels. While emergency measures provide short-term relief, they do not address the root causes of pollution. Courts have interpreted the right to life to include living in a pollution-free environment, allowing citizens to seek redress. However, the enforcement of these rights and standards is lacking in many places.

title: Why Siraj's absence from Wellington Test is harsh but not a surprise
description: When asked about Siraj's exclusion, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak asserted that they played the XI the management felt best suited for these conditions. Kotak further added that Siraj remains world-class and said there was nothing wrong with the bowler that led to his omission from the Wellington Test.

title: Denmark buckles under Trump, approves US military expansion deal in Greenland
description: Denmark's parliament has sanctioned a pivotal security agreement that broadens the scope of U.S. military involvement in Greenland. This agreement not only updates current defense installations but also facilitates the creation of new military infrastructure. Amid rising global tensions, it bolsters American missile defense in the Arctic, emphasizing Greenland's strategic role in monitoring military movements in key regions while maintaining its sovereignty.

title: Noida couple pays Rs 25L for dream plot, builder sells it to another; court orders refund
description: Bajwa Developers Ltd has been ordered by the commission to refund Rs 25.2 lakh along with interest. The complaint was filed by a couple who faced delays and issues with their plot purchase. They discovered that their allotted plot had been sold to someone else at a higher price. Despite full payment, possession was not handed over, leading to the legal complaint.

title: Anthropic IPO: How can Indian investors buy shares in Claude's parent company
description: Anthropic has made headlines by securing a staggering $81.31 billion in its IPO, breaking previous records. Indian investors who missed the initial offering will now need to wait for the trading phase to commence. Shares will be obtainable through overseas brokerage accounts, leveraging the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme, which allows for remittances of up to $250,000 per year for foreign investments like US stocks.

title: Jasprit Bumrah and the rest: The familiar storyline replays at Basin Reserve
description: Jasprit Bumrah gave India the perfect start, but a familiar story unfolded at the Basin Reserve as the rest of the attack failed to sustain the pressure. Centurion Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips capitalised on India's lapses, exposing the limitations of the inexperienced bowling attack.

title: 'Chaos if major powers clash': Xi's blunt warning at trilateral with Trump, Putin
Melinda French Gates' $240m almost awarded; 91% to groups new to Pivotal
description: In 2024, Melinda French Gates launched the Global Leaders programme, allocating $240 million to empower 12 notable leaders. Most of the grants were earmarked for emerging organizations that previously lacked funding. While leaders like Alfiee Breland-Noble established funds for various initiatives, others such as Jacinda Ardern introduced innovative maternal health programs. This initiative aspires to explore trust-based philanthropy, with a comprehensive report due next year to showcase the outcomes.

title: Malaysia to not remain visa free for Indian visitors from Jan 1, 2027
description: Malaysia will end the visa exemption policy for Indian tourists beginning on January 1, 2027. This decision comes after an increase in Indians misusing the visa-free entry for employment purposes. The High Commission of India in Kuala Lumpur has issued warnings regarding these violations of immigration rules. Indian nationals must obtain a valid visa prior to travelling to Malaysia from this date onward.

title: HC: Why only royals? Keep Mumbai clean for citizens too
description: Bombay High Court questioned the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation regarding temporary cleanliness efforts for royal guests. The bench emphasized the need for consistent cleanliness for Mumbai's residents instead of short-term measures. It raised concerns over plastic pollution and the city's garbage management. The judges highlighted the ongoing issues related to waste disposal and requested an audit of the Kanjurmarg facility. A follow-up report is expected to be submitted by December 7.

title: Coyote may be first to cross $114m California wildlife bridge before opening
description: In an exciting development, a coyote has been spotted utilizing a newly constructed wildlife bridge spanning California's US 101 Freeway. This innovative structure is designed to reconnect fragmented habitats caused by highways and urbanization. Researchers are actively observing wildlife interactions with the bridge through remote cameras, aiming to enhance the migration of various species, such as mountain lions and deer.
